title: Turning a panic into an error
hints: recover() stops a panic, but only when it's called directly inside a deferred function. It returns the value passed to panic, or nil if there was no panic.
Give Safely a named result err. A deferred closure can then set err after recovering.
func Safely(f func()) (err error) { defer func() { if r := recover(); r != nil { err = fmt.Errorf("recovered: %v", r) } }(); f(); return nil }
